title: sequence-boundary-fuzzing-log
content:
Goal:
Short fuzzing run to exercise sequence-boundary edge-cases that cause inconsistent KV offsets and attention-kernel fallbacks under continuous-batching. Aim: capture a small, deterministic repro and list hypotheses + quick mitigations to try in next oncall window.

Background/context:
- Repro class seen in prod: long contexts with interleaved short requests cause occasional 'kv-offset drift' that manifests later as either out-of-range KV reads or when attention kernel selection flips to a slower fallback.
- Observed most frequently with mixed seqlen distribution (some requests ~64 tokens, others random long prefixes 2048-8192) while batching/route-merging enabled.
- A lot of previous notes exist; this is a focused fuzz + log collection attempt.

What I ran (commands, scripts):
1) small reproducer harness (repo: runtime/tools/seq-fuzz)
- python3 seq_fuzz.py --model rdx-13b-quant --batcher continuous --max-iter 2500 --seqlen-dist "mix:0.7@64,0.3@[1024:8192]" --kv-cap 131072 --seed 1793 --save-trace /tmp/sf_trace.json

2) quick one-off curl to hosted test endpoint (to reproduce same pattern via API):
- for i in $(seq 1 200); do 
    LEN=$(( (RANDOM % 2 == 0) ? 64 : (1024 + RANDOM % 7168) ));
    echo "{\"input\":\"$(head -c $LEN /dev/urandom | base64)\"}" | 
    curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3100/v1/complete -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @- >/dev/null;
  done

3) kernel-selection tracing (built into runtime debug flags):
- export REDWOOD_DEBUG_KERNELS=1; ./runtime_server --config debug.yml 2>&1 | tee /tmp/runtime-debug.log

Key error snippets captured:
- Trace file excerpt (sf_trace.json):
  timestamp: 2024-11-04T09:23:12.452Z, request_id: r-3f9a, event: apply_kv_patch, kv_index_write: 131072, kv_capacity: 131072, note: "index == capacity -> wrapped?"
  later: RuntimeError: KV read out-of-range: requested=131072, capacity=131072

- runtime-debug.log excerpt: 
  [09:23:12.447] selected_kernel=flash_attn_v2 seq_len=8192 batch_size=1 memory_est=9.8GB
  [09:23:12.450] kernel_fallback: triton_attention_naive reason="memory_est>node_limit"
  [09:23:12.451] batch_merge: merged_request_ids=[r-3f9a,r-77bb] continuous_batch_id=cb-521
  [09:23:12.452] kvcache: prefix_eviction triggered seq_len_boundary=8192 evict_to_offset=131000
  [09:23:12.453] kv_offset_map: { session_id:s-109 offset:130995 }

- Observed race pattern: eviction callback runs concurrently with KV append when continuous-batcher merge completes -> both update the global per-session 'append_index' without proper CAS -> momentary inconsistent view allowing append index == capacity -> later read fails.

Quick reproducer (minimal Python snippet used in harness):
- pseudocode: 
  def append_kv(session, kv_chunk):
      off = session.append_index
      session.kv_storage[off:off+len(kv_chunk)] = kv_chunk
      session.append_index = off + len(kv_chunk)

  def eviction_cb(session, target_offset):
      # naive shrink
      session.append_index = min(session.append_index, target_offset)

  # race: append_kv running concurrently with eviction_cb -> append_index can be set to wrapped value if interleaving occurs

Hypotheses:
1) Off-by-one when eviction computes 'evict_to_offset' at capacity boundary; code uses capacity as inclusive endpoint somewhere. Edge case: if evict_to_offset == capacity, subsequent append uses capacity as write index -> out-of-range.
2) Missing atomic update / lock around per-session append_index during concurrent append + eviction. Continuous-batcher (merge code) and eviction run on different worker threads.
3) Kernel selection path depends on estimated memory after kvcache accounting. If kvcache eviction hasn't completed but append has tentatively increased offset, kernel estimator sees higher memory use and flips to fallback kernel. The fallback then runs slower and increases batching window -> exacerbates races.
4) Pathological seqlen distribution (many long tails) more likely to trigger because evict_to_offset computations are done using 'max_recent_seq' heuristic which biases eviction to larger offsets.

Notes on attention kernel selection oddity:
- I saw inconsistent logging where selected_kernel first chosen as flash_attn_v2 then immediately 'kernel_fallback' to triton_attention_naive. The fallback reason often cited 'memory_est>node_limit' but memory_est changes between the two calls. Suspect parallel accounting updates from kvcache instrumentation.
- Actionable probe: add a local consistent snapshot for kernel selection (read-only copy of session accounting) and see if flip rate drops.

Attempts & results so far (what I tried):
- Add coarse-grained lock around session.append_index: repro rate dropped by ~95% in harness (from ~1/200 to ~1/4000). However coarse lock impacts latency for small requests when a long request holds the lock -> unacceptable.
- Change eviction to compute evict_to_offset = max(0, append_index - capacity + safety_margin) instead of using capacity directly. Reduced hits but didn't eliminate them.
- Instrumented kernel selection to log a snapshot of kvcache accounting (pre/post). This shows accounting sometimes lags by 2-3 events.

Next experiments to try (priority ordered):
1) Implement CAS-style update for append_index (atomic compare-and-swap) with small optimistic retry loop; measure latency impact.
2) Add single-writer guarantee per session via lightweight sharded mutex keyed by session_id (avoid global locks). Test at 10k qps harness.
3) Make kernel selection use a stable accounting snapshot: compute mem_est using a read-copy of kvcache index and pending_evictions queue. Re-run fuzz.
4) Add invariant checks in debug builds: on append, assert(append_index+len <= capacity) and log context if violated. Turn on in prod limited-sample mode.
5) Tighten eviction math: never return evict_to_offset == capacity (force -1) and ensure wrap detection path handles equal-to-capacity as wrap-to-zero case.

Observations about reproducer quality and tuning: 
- Seeded fuzz (seed=1793) is reliably producing 1-3 failures in 2500 iterations with current master. After coarse-lock, failures drop to ~0-1 / 10k iterations.
- Failures usually occur shortly after a long request (~>4k) is merged with a short request in the same continuous batch.
- If I disable continuous batching (batcher=none) no failures seen in 10k iterations -> strong evidence continuous-batching merge/eviction interplay is the root cause.

Temporary mitigations for oncall: 
- If a production region shows increased KV OOR errors, flip continuous_batching=off for the affected runtime pool and restart workers gradually. That will reduce throughput but restore correctness.
- Deploy a debug build with the invariant checks enabled and ring-fence logs for sample sessions to capture full traces.

Questions for follow-up with SRE/Runtime team:
- Is there a low-latency atomic primitive we can use for per-session append_index that doesn't require a heap allocation? (Lock-free CAS preferred)
- Can continuous-batcher be configured to avoid merging long+short requests (simple heuristic based on req.seq_len) as a short-term safety?
- Are there plan/benchmarks for kernel selection stabilization (snapshot approach) in APs?

To do (next steps, owner):
- [ ] Maya: implement CAS update in small branch and push PR for perf regression testing (target: perf/bench 5000 qps test).
- [ ] Arjun: prototype session-sharded mutex and run load test with real traffic replay (owner: Arjun).
- [ ] Sofia: add kernel-selection snapshot instrumentation and add to debug logging.
- [ ] Maya: prepare a short runbook entry for oncall with steps for flipping continuous_batching and enabling debug instrumentation.

Attachments/where traces are saved:
- /tmp/sf_trace.json (seed 1793 run)
- /tmp/runtime-debug.log (kernel and kvcache traces)
- tests/results/2024-11-07/fuzz-summary.md

Random notes / freeform ideas:
- Could we add a small per-session 'pending_eviction' flag that prevents append from proceeding if eviction is in-flight? Might be simpler than shipping CAS right away. But need to evaluate tail-latency impact.
- Also consider bounding kernel selection flips per-request: if a request's kernel flips within 10ms window, prefer the first choice to reduce churn.

End of scratchpad.

If anyone reading wants to reproduce quickly: checkout runtime branch sequence-fuzz, run seq_fuzz.py with the flags above, watch /tmp/runtime-debug.log. Happy to walk through in standup or pair on the CAS PR.
